Gaussian splats in three dimensions

Source: R/layers-splat.R
geom_splat_3d.Rd

Draw point clouds with Gaussian footprints, or render Gaussian captures read by read_points_3d(). Each row is one Gaussian.

Usage

geom_splat_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  ...,
  sh_degree = NULL,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, ..., show.legend, inherit.aes

As in geom_point_3d().

sh_degree

Maximum spherical-harmonic degree, from 0 to 3. NULL uses all available coefficients.

Details

size is an isotropic standard deviation in data units (default 0.02). scale_x, scale_y, scale_z give anisotropic standard deviations; qw, qx, qy, qz give a rotation quaternion, normalised internally. Mapped size follows the usual size scale; use I(size) to keep data units. The other covariance aesthetics are used directly.

Unmapped properties are read from INRIA-format 3D Gaussian splatting columns: scale_0 through scale_2 are exponentiated, opacity is logistic-transformed, and rot_0 through rot_3 are normalised. f_dc_0 through f_dc_2 and optional channel-major f_rest_* coefficients give camera-dependent RGB colour. Explicit colour or fill overrides these coefficients. Ordinary colour and fill scales and colour = I(hex) work as for points.

Raster, vector and hybrid panels use depth-composited EWA footprints truncated at three standard deviations. Path tracing uses Gaussian responses along rays with the colour as surface albedo. The viewer and scene exports display coloured points. The stroke-only plotter omits splats. Splats require an affine Cartesian frame and position scales.

References

Kerbl et al. (2023). 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering. doi:10.1145/3592433 .

Zwicker et al. (2002). EWA Splatting. doi:10.1109/TVCG.2002.1021576 .

Moenne-Loccoz et al. (2024). 3D Gaussian Ray Tracing: Fast Tracing of Particle Scenes. doi:10.1145/3687934 .

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 12),
                 y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 12))
d$z <- with(d, 0.2 * cos(3 * x) * sin(3 * y))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, colour = z)) +
  geom_splat_3d(size = 0.12) + coord_3d()
